items.q: I went to Neeka's and jammed with Freddie. One morning I met a trumpeter named Arthur Briggs in the Hot Feet

ctx.x: The day after, we started rehearsing the show we had done in Monte Carlo with a French orchestra at the Rex theater. This was the largest theater I had ever seen or played in. There was plenty of space for the show at the Sporting d'Ete and it was the same at the Rex because the two bands were on the stage opposite each other and we still seemed to be a mile apart. In a few days, I learned how to walk from my hotel to the Rex. I met a journalist named Edgar Higgins who wrote for the Chicago Defender under the…

There were quite a few American negros in Paris and many of them made the Hotel Liseux their meeting place. There was an American negro girl singer named Neeka Shaw who had a cabaret where a fine pianist by the name of Freddie Johnson was playing. I had heard some musicians in New York speak about Freddie Johnson and he was everything I had heard about him concerning his piano playing. Neeka's place was called the Hot Feet and was on Rue Pigalle 53.

I went to Neeka's and jammed with Freddie. One morning I met a trumpeter named Arthur Briggs in the Hot Feet but we had met before in New York when Briggs was there in 1931 with Noble Sissle at the Lafayette. Sissle also had a fine young first trumpet named Joe Keys with him.
